issues.body: Bead 2 still defines `worker_no_change_max_unattributed` as an integer with default `0` and says only that it needs no float-branch edit. In the current `_thresholds_of`, every non-curator threshold other than `worker_success_floor` must be a non-boolean integer strictly greater than zero. Thus an explicit policy override of the documented zero boundary raises `must be a positive integer`. The design still does not specify the dedicated validation rule or boundary tests needed to make its recommended fail-closed setting implementable.
issues.fix_hint: Require a dedicated `_thresholds_of` case for `worker_no_change_max_unattributed` that accepts non-boolean integers `>= 0` (and define an upper bound if one is intended). Add acceptance criteria proving that `0` is accepted while `-1`, booleans, and non-integers are rejected.
issues.title: The zero unattributed threshold remains incompatible with policy validation

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-4 major finding remains materially unchanged. Bead 2 still specifies `worker_no_change_max_unattributed` with a default and meaningful boundary of `0`, but only says that it needs no float-branch edit. The current validator's generic integer branch rejects zero, and the acceptance criteria still omit tests for this policy boundary. Consequently the recommended fail-closed default cannot be explicitly configured. Progress is stagnant because the same major issue persists at the same severity.
